title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for breast cancer and liver metastasis management.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is a 51-year-old female with a known malignant neoplasm of the right breast. She is currently receiving chemotherapy and was stable at the previous visit. She reports managing fatigue and mild nausea associated with her current regimen.

[Update] Patient presents today for a follow-up regarding her progress. She reports that she is currently receiving chemotherapy for the cancer of the right breast. She notes increased fatigue over the last two weeks but denies significant nausea or vomiting. She reports mild abdominal discomfort, which she attributes to the liver metastasis. She denies any new-onset fevers, chills, or acute shortness of breath.

Medication List:
- Cyclophosphamide/Doxorubicin (Chemotherapy)
- Ondansetron 8mg as needed for nausea
- Multivitamin daily

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 78, SpO2 98% on RA, Temp 98.6 F, Weight 165 lbs.

Recent Labs:
- Hemoglobin: 11.2 g/dL
- White Blood Cell Count: 3.8 x 10^9/L
- Platelets: 145 x 10^3/uL
- ALT: 88 U/L
- AST: 76 U/L
- Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
- eGFR: >90 mL/min/1.73m2

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fatigue. Negative for fever, chills, or weight loss.
Gastrointestinal: Positive for mild abdominal discomfort. Negative for diarrhea or constipation.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain or weakness.
Neurological: Negative for headaches or dizziness.
Skin: Negative for new rashes.

Social History: Patient lives with her spouse and two children. She works part-time as a freelance editor. She denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History: Mother had breast cancer at age 55. Father had hypertension.

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears tired but in no acute distress.
Breast: Exam of the right breast shows a palpable mass. Skin is intact without erythema.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. Mild tenderness noted in the RUQ.
Extremities: No edema noted.

Assessment:
1. Cancer of the right breast, currently receiving chemotherapy.
2. Liver metastasis, currently stable but requiring monitoring of liver function tests.

Plan:
1. Continue current chemotherapy regimen as scheduled.
2. Monitor liver function tests every 2 weeks to track the liver metastasis.
3. Provide supportive care for fatigue and abdominal discomfort.
4. Follow up in 4 weeks for repeat labs and clinical evaluation.

Electronically signed,
J. Lindqvist, NP
May 14, 2026
explanations: Cancer of the right female breast under current treatment is a current malignancy: C50.911.
Liver metastases: C78.7, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver (HCC 17).

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
The note documents the right breast: use the right-breast code.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in the liver, not bone.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Lung/Liver/Brain/and Other Organs; Acute Myeloid Leukemia Except Promyelocytic
